# future.mizu: Parallel Future Backend using ‘mizu’

> **Note:** This package is an early prototype under development.

## Introduction

The **[future](https://cran.r-project.org/package=future)** package
provides a generic API for using futures in R. A future is a simple yet
powerful mechanism to evaluate an R expression and retrieve its value at
some point in time. Futures can be resolved in many different ways
depending on which strategy is used. There are various types of
synchronous and asynchronous futures to choose from in the
**[future](https://cran.r-project.org/package=future)** package.

This package,
**[future.mizu](https://github.com/futureverse/future.mizu)**, provides
a type of futures that utilizes the
**[mizu](https://cran.r-project.org/package=mizu)** package.

For example,

\
[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(`[`future`](https://future.futureverse.org)`)`\
[`plan`](https://future.futureverse.org/reference/plan.html)`(``future.mizu``::`[`mizu_multisession`](https://future.mizu.futureverse.org/reference/mizu_multisession.md)`)`\
\
`x`` `[`%<-%`](https://future.futureverse.org/reference/futureAssign.html)` ``{`` `[`Sys.sleep`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/Sys.sleep.html)`(``5``)``; ``3.14`` ``}`\
`y`` `[`%<-%`](https://future.futureverse.org/reference/futureAssign.html)` ``{`` `[`Sys.sleep`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/Sys.sleep.html)`(``5``)``; ``2.71`` ``}`\
`x`` ``+`` ``y`\
`#> [1] 5.85`

This is obviously a toy example to illustrate what futures look like and
how to work with them. For further examples on how to use futures, see
the vignettes of the
**[future](https://cran.r-project.org/package=future)** package as well
as those of
**[future.apply](https://cran.r-project.org/package=future.apply)**,
**[furrr](https://cran.r-project.org/package=furrr)**, and
**[doFuture](https://cran.r-project.org/package=doFuture)**. You can
also use **[futurize](https://cran.r-project.org/package=futurize)** to
parallelize your existing map-reduce code,
e.g. `lapply(xs, fcn) |> futurize()`.

## Using the future.mizu backend

The **future.mizu** package implements a **future** backend wrapper for
**mizu**.

| Backend | Description | Alternative in future package |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `mizu_multisession` | parallel evaluation in separate R processes (on current machine) | `plan(multisession)` |

### Advantages of mizu futures

The **mizu** package runs parallel R workers on the local machine, where
the main R process and the workers communicate via shared memory (POSIX
shared memory on Linux and macOS, and Win32 file mappings on Windows)
instead of through sockets. Communication is cheap enough that work can
be divided into small pieces, and large vectors and data frames can be
read in place, without being copied. The `mizu_multisession` futures
make these properties available to everything that is built on the
Future API, e.g. **future.apply**, **furrr**, **doFuture**, and
**futurize**, without having to change any code.

Because of this, `mizu_multisession` futures behave like any other
future: the code does not have to change, the results are identical, and
output and conditions, e.g. [`cat()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/cat.html),
[`message()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/message.html), and
[`warning()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/warning.html), are relayed to the
main R session as usual.

### Limitations

- The workers always run on the local machine. For workers on other
  machines, or on a high-performance compute (HPC) cluster, use another
  **future** backend.

- At most 64 workers are supported by **mizu**.

- Cancelling a future is advisory. A future that is already running on a
  worker cannot be interrupted; it runs to completion and its result is
  discarded.

- Using a single worker,
  `plan(future.mizu::mizu_multisession, workers = 1)`, falls back to
  sequential processing in the current R process, unless the number of
  workers is protected by [`I()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/AsIs.html),
  e.g. `workers = I(1)`.

## Demos

The **[future](https://cran.r-project.org/package=future)** package
provides a demo using futures for calculating a set of Mandelbrot
planes. The demo does not assume anything about what type of futures are
used. *The user has full control of how futures are evaluated*. For
instance, to use `mizu_multisession` futures, run the demo as:

\
[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(`[`future`](https://future.futureverse.org)`)`\
[`plan`](https://future.futureverse.org/reference/plan.html)`(``future.mizu``::`[`mizu_multisession`](https://future.mizu.futureverse.org/reference/mizu_multisession.md)`)`\
\
[`demo`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/demo.html)`(``"mandelbrot"``, package ``=`` ``"future"``, ask ``=`` ``FALSE``)`

## Installation

The package is not yet available on CRAN. To install the development
version from GitHub, use:

\
`remotes``::`[`install_github`](https://remotes.r-lib.org/reference/install_github.html)`(``"futureverse/future.mizu"``)`

This will install the package from source.
